\paragraph{Direction asymmetry and quality confounding.}
The formality axis exhibits a pronounced direction asymmetry: the judge selects the formal variant in 78.8\% of formal-is-rewrite pairs ($p = 0.001$) but only 54.5\% of casual-is-rewrite pairs ($p = 0.83$).
One explanation is that formally written texts are inherently perceived as higher quality, so original quality $Q$ and formality $S$ are partially confounded.
Logistic decomposition (exp-014) estimates an original-preference odds ratio of $\text{OR} = 1.82$ ($p = 0.052$, GEE), confirming that this confound is non-negligible even after position control.
The NLI gate blocks \emph{content} changes but cannot block quality perception shifts that are themselves mediated by style---a fundamental identifiability limit of any text-rewriting approach.
Future work should incorporate human quality ratings of both original and rewritten texts to disentangle the $S \to Y$ and $Q \to Y$ pathways.

\paragraph{Single judge and benchmark.}
All experiments use GPT-4o as the sole judge and LLMBar as the evaluation benchmark.
Multi-judge experiments (Claude, Gemini) and multi-benchmark extensions are in progress; until replicated, our findings are specific to this judge--benchmark configuration.

The NLI gate validation (\S\ref{sec:nli_validation}) uses Qwen3-32B as annotator rather than human judges.

\paragraph{Style Bias Detection and Mitigation}
The foundational LLM-as-judge framework was established by \citet{zheng2023judging}, who introduced MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena and documented position bias in pairwise evaluation.
\citet{wang2023faireval} further showed that preference rankings can be manipulated by swapping option order, proposing a win/tie/lose annotation scheme.
\citet{li2024calibraeval} address selection bias through calibration of prediction distributions during inference.
These works focus on \emph{position} bias and calibration; style bias as a separate, dominant bias source has received attention only recently \citep{murugadoss2025sos,li2026preference,soumik2026judging}.
Multi-feature frameworks such as CASSE \citep{casse2026concise} and FairJudge \citep{wang2026fairjudge} decompose style into finer dimensions but rely on correlational analyses without interventional controls.

\paragraph{Bradley-Terry Models in Evaluation}
The Bradley-Terry model \citep{bradley1952rank} underpins modern LLM evaluation platforms including Chatbot Arena \citep{zheng2023judging} and AlpacaFarm \citep{dubois2023alpacafarm}.
We adopt BT as our primary pairwise analysis because it uses all comparison data---including position-inconsistent pairs---without requiring a consistency filter, yielding proper effect-size confidence intervals that sign tests cannot provide.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We introduced Causal Style Decomposition (CSD), a black-box framework for detecting per-axis style bias in LLM judges through style-controlled rewriting, NLI-based content gating, and position-controlled pairwise comparison.
Applying CSD to GPT-4o on a formality axis, we uncovered the Likert Blindspot: a two-layer measurement limitation in which integer discretization produces ${\sim}60\%$ uninformative ties, and even non-tied absolute scores capture weaker signal than forced pairwise comparison.
A sensitivity hierarchy across seven statistical methods---from Bradley-Terry modeling to ordinal regression---confirms that the Blindspot is inherent to Likert measurement, not an artifact of any particular test.

These findings carry practical implications for the evaluation community.
Style bias audits that rely on Likert scoring risk systematic underestimation of bias magnitude; pairwise comparison should be the default measurement protocol for per-axis bias detection.
Existing Likert-based results, including those from RATE and similar frameworks, may need reexamination under pairwise measurement to assess whether reported null findings reflect genuine absence of bias or measurement insensitivity.
Future work should extend CSD to multiple judges, additional style axes, and larger evaluation benchmarks to establish the generality of both the framework and the Likert Blindspot.

**CRITICAL：§3.2 L18 NLI 方向描述与实现完全相反**

当前写 "Bidirectional verification is essential for axes that inherently change information density (e.g., verbosity)" —— 这是错的。

事实：
- Bidirectional NLI 在 verbosity 上 FAIL（65% pass，D012）
- 修复方案是 direction-aware NLI（86% pass，D013）：expansion 用 backward NLI only，compression 用 forward NLI only
- 对于不改变信息量的轴（formality, register），使用标准 bidirectional verification

正确描述：
> "For axes that preserve information density (formality, register), we apply standard bidirectional entailment. For axes that inherently change information density (e.g., verbosity), bidirectional verification is inappropriate—expansion necessarily introduces new content that the original cannot entail. We instead apply direction-aware verification: for expansions, only backward entailment (counterfactual entails original); for compressions, only forward entailment (original entails counterfactual). This recovered verbosity from 65\% to 86\% pass rate."

**WARNING 1：§3.1 "symmetric pair" 措辞**
改为 "balanced across both directions at the dataset level"。每个文本只改写一次（基于检测到的原始风格），不是 per-text symmetric。

**WARNING 2：补充 style detection 步骤**
§3.1 开头加一步：原始文本风格由 Qwen3-32B 检测（binary classification: formal/casual），检测结果决定改写方向。

**WARNING 3：补充 double-rewrite / RATE 描述**
§3.1 末尾加：为控制 rewriting artifact bias，对每个 counterfactual 再做一次 same-style rewrite（double-rewrite），形成 original ↔ double-rewrite 对照组。引用 exp-014 的 RATE bias correction。

**WARNING 4：补充数据集描述**
§3.3 或新建 §3.5 Experimental Setup：LLMBar benchmark（Zeng et al. 2023），n=100 instruction-response pairs，涵盖多种任务类型。说明为什么选 LLMBar（设计用于评测 LLM judge 的辨别力，包含 human-verified quality labels）。

We isolate the causal effect of individual style attributes on judge scores by generating text pairs that differ along exactly one style axis.
Given an input text, an instruction-tuned LLM (Qwen3-32B, temperature 0.7) rewrites it according to an axis-specific prompt (e.g., ``Rewrite the following text to be more formal/casual while preserving the exact same content and meaning'').
For each axis, we produce both a forward rewrite (original $\to$ target style) and a backward rewrite (target $\to$ original style) to form a symmetric pair.
This bidirectional design controls for asymmetric effects: a text shortened for conciseness may lose information that an expansion would not.
tool_args.new_string:
We isolate the effect of individual style attributes on judge scores by generating text pairs that differ along exactly one style axis.
For each text, an instruction-tuned LLM (Qwen3-32B) first classifies its current style along the target axis (e.g., formal vs.\ casual via binary classification), then rewrites it toward the opposite pole (temperature 0.7) according to an axis-specific prompt (e.g., ``Rewrite the following text to be more formal/casual while preserving the exact same content and meaning'').
This produces a dataset balanced across both directions at the dataset level: texts detected as formal are rewritten to casual, and vice versa.
